problem: IL-based VLN agents overfit the teacher's biased behavior and generalize poorly, while IL+RL hybrids still need expensive trajectory or action annotations and suffer from sparse rewards.
motivation: Better generalization without costly labels requires decomposing long navigation into simpler subproblems. Subgoals unconstrained by predefined semantics may be more generalizable than hand-defined ones.
key_idea: A hierarchical RL agent in which a manager generates unconstrained intrinsic subgoals and a worker uses subgoal-driven attention to predict actions, with a history-aware discriminator supplying intrinsic rewards and self-supervision.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that self-supervising the worker with manager-generated subgoals removes the need for labeled actions, and that the discriminator's intrinsic rewards ease reward sparsity.
method: Manager (high-level agent): decomposes the complex navigation task into simple intrinsic subgoals, with no constraint on subgoal semantics.
Worker (low-level agent): uses an intrinsic subgoal-driven attention mechanism to predict actions in a smaller state space.
History-aware discriminator (HAD): incorporates historical information into subgoal discrimination and gives the worker additional intrinsic rewards to alleviate reward sparsity.
Self-supervision: the manager's generated subgoals supervise the worker, so no labeled actions are needed.
